shots.purpose: Put the impossible loss on screen first: the great ship going down by the bow
shots.claim: the Titanic sank in under three hours despite contemporary claims she was practically unsinkable
shots.evidence: full-bleed night-sea plate: ship silhouette bow-down, iceberg standing off, 1912 engraved style
shots.motion_reason: slow push toward the bow-down silhouette so the loss is immediate
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the timeline of the night

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment engraving-style plate: Titanic silhouette bow-down with iceberg on the horizon

one_second.relationship: the unsinkable ship is going down

shots.purpose: Make the night a clock: sighting, thirty-seven seconds, impact
shots.claim: the lookouts reported the iceberg at 11:40 PM on April 14, 1912, about thirty-seven seconds before impact
shots.evidence: timeline card: clock face at 11:40, a 37-second gap marked, impact marker at the starboard bow
shots.motion_reason: slow drift along the timeline so the 37 seconds feel short

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment timeline card: clock face reading 11:40 with a short 37-second gap to an impact marker

one_second.relationship: the warning window was under a minute

shots.purpose: Reconstruct the damage: six forward compartments opened along the hull
shots.claim: the collision breached the first six forward compartments along about three hundred feet of hull
shots.evidence: hull side-profile reconstruction: six forward compartments outlined and hatched, buckled plate marks along the seam line
shots.motion_reason: lateral drift along the hull so the wound reads as one long line
shots.transition_reason: cut to the overflow chain the damage triggers

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment hull profile: ship side view with six hatched forward compartments

one_second.relationship: the damage is a chain of rooms, not one hole

shots.purpose: Show the failure mechanism: water spilling compartment to compartment over a D-deck line
shots.claim: the watertight bulkheads rose only to D deck, so water spilled from full compartments into the next
shots.evidence: overflow chain card: four compartment boxes with water levels rising, dashed D-deck line above, spill arrows over each wall
shots.motion_reason: held framing; the rising levels and spill arrows carry the mechanism
shots.transition_reason: dip to white into the design decision (act pivot)

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram: four compartment boxes filling with water, spill arrows over D-deck line

one_second.relationship: each full compartment becomes the next one's flood

shots.purpose: Show the mistake: two drawings, the approved one with ten feet less margin
shots.claim: design revisions before approval lowered the watertight bulkhead height by roughly ten feet from the earlier drawings
shots.evidence: side-by-side design cards: earlier drawing with taller bulkheads (dashed extension) versus approved drawing with the cut height, minus-ten-feet callout between
shots.motion_reason: slow push on the gap between the two heights

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment comparison card: two bulkhead profiles with a height difference callout

one_second.relationship: the approved ship had less margin than the designed one

shots.purpose: Land the cost: two thousand two hundred aboard, seven hundred and five saved
shots.claim: the Titanic foundered two hours and forty minutes after the collision; of roughly two thousand two hundred aboard, seven hundred and five survived
shots.evidence: count card: tall column of 2,200 person marks against a short column of 705, scale difference visible at a glance
shots.motion_reason: near-static so the scale contrast carries the beat

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment count card: tall mark-column for 2,200 against short mark-column for 705

one_second.relationship: the saved are a small fraction of the aboard

shots.purpose: Resolve the hook: the margin line lit along the hull, the flaw that was built in
shots.claim: the loss of designed safety margin, not the iceberg alone, is what sank the Titanic
shots.evidence: dusk reprise of the opening silhouette, calm sea, the hull margin line lit warm where the compartments failed
shots.motion_reason: slow pull-out, the frame settles with the argument

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment-plate ship silhouette reprise with a lit hull margin line, calm sea

one_second.relationship: the flaw was in the design, not the sea
